task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper and terminal on the floor)
role labels derived from play-by-play play-type possessions
separability of coverage from talent and role-player counts
methodological_questions: Does coverage vary within team enough to be studied?
Is coverage separable from talent and from role-player counts?
Does the talent control behave (sign, stability, placebo)?
Are the role labels reliable, and are they derived from outcomes?
Is power adequate given lineup sparsity and possession clustering?
Do role labels and talent estimates leak information from the outcome period?
evidence_establishes: Nothing. retrieve_history returned zero records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether earlier project work defined or validated organizer, shaper and terminal roles.
Whether coverage was previously found to vary within team or to be separable from talent.
Whether any talent control was tried before, or how it behaved.
Whether any approach has already failed.
own_inferences: Coverage is likely to vary within team. Rotations mix starters and bench units, so the 'at least one of each role' indicator should not be constant, unless the role definitions are so broad that nearly every lineup is covered (a ceiling effect).

If roles are assigned to players, then coverage is a deterministic function of which players are on the floor. It will correlate strongly with the number of role-holders and with the minutes-weighted talent of the lineup. Separability is therefore the main substantive risk, not variation.

The question has three parts: variation, separability and a well-behaved talent control. These are measurement-validity diagnostics, not a causal-effect test. 'Behaves' must be turned into explicit numeric criteria before any analysis, or the question cannot be falsified.

The 90 team-seasons are probably 30 teams across 2022-23 to 2024-25. 2025-26 may be partly or wholly outside the count. The 420,993 possessions are a larger and clustered unit, so the effective sample size for team-level claims is far smaller.
uncertainties: How organizer, shaper and terminal are operationalised, and whether the thresholds use outcomes such as points.
Which talent measure will be used, and whether it is built from the same possessions as the outcome.
Whether 2025-26 data are in the 90 team-seasons or serve as a holdout.
The distribution of possessions per lineup, which is not stated.
What 'behaves' means for the talent control (expected sign, stability across seasons, placebo null).

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval was empty, so history could not change the decision. The decision rests only on the task statement and general methodological reasoning. The absence of records is not evidence that the question is new or unanswered.

blocking_constraints.text: If role labels or coverage use points or efficiency, then separability from talent and any later outcome link is circular. Labels must use non-outcome actions such as initiation, passes and shot location.

Coverage is a mechanical function of how many role-holders are on the floor and of the role definitions. Separability from counts cannot be shown by regression alone. It needs conditioning on the count, or a comparison against a null model with the same counts.

prior_work.summary: No earlier project work was returned. It is unknown whether this question, or any part of it, has been addressed.

risks.text: Coverage is deterministic given role assignment and counts. High coverage mostly reflects having more role-holders. A raw coverage-versus-count correlation is expected and does not show inseparability by itself.

Coach lineup selection ties coverage to talent, minutes, opponent, starters-versus-bench status and garbage time. Collinearity between coverage, talent and counts may make separate effects unidentifiable.
Play-type labels from the derived graph database, and any role thresholds that depend on points, can bake the outcome into the exposure.
Roles come from play-by-play inference and may be noisy for low-usage players. Role assignment may flip across seasons or halves. Misclassification attenuates variation and separability estimates.

Roles and talent estimated on the full season, then applied to the same season's lineups, use future information. The talent control must be estimated out of sample, for example from prior seasons or an odd/even-game split.
Many five-man lineups have few possessions. Lineup-level coverage variation can be dominated by tiny units.
There are only 90 team-seasons, and possessions are clustered within lineups, games and teams. Within-team variance components and talent-control stability have wide intervals.

Talent control 'behaving' requires a placebo, such as permuted role labels or a talent measure shifted to another team, that returns a null. Without it, a plausible-looking talent coefficient is uninformative.
Pace, spacing and role definitions drift across 2022-26. Pooled estimates may mix regimes.
Several role combinations, thresholds, talent measures and seasons create forking paths unless fixed in advance.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified diagnostics. (1) Within-team variation: the share of variance in lineup coverage (binary, plus a continuous role-minutes coverage score) that lies within team-season rather than between, as an intraclass correlation, with 95% CI. (2) Separability: the partial association of coverage with outcomes or lineup features after conditioning on role-holder counts and lineup talent. Assess it with variance inflation factors, a condition number, and the share of coverage variance not explained by counts and talent, as the residual R-squared from regressing coverage on those two. (3) Talent-control behaviour: the sign, out-of-sample stability and placebo null of the talent coefficient.
design.unit: Lineup-stint within team-season, weighted by possessions. Team-season is the cluster, and the sensitivity analysis uses team-season aggregates (n=90).
design.sample: Fit on 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season, excluding garbage time and keeping lineups above a pre-set possession minimum (for example 50, with sensitivity at 25 and 100). Playoffs are analysed separately. 2025-26 is a confirmatory holdout, used only if its completeness date is respected and it is frozen before any fitting. Roles and talent are estimated only on data preceding or independent of the evaluated possessions, using prior-season or odd/even-game splits.
design.power: There are 90 team-seasons, so only large between-team effects are detectable at team level. Possession-level power is limited by clustering, and the effective sample size is closer to the number of distinct lineups and teams. Before looking at outcomes, compute the design effect and the minimum detectable ICC and partial R-squared by simulation or a cluster bootstrap. Declare the question underpowered for any effect below that threshold.
design.controls: Role-holder counts, minutes-weighted lineup talent from an out-of-sample measure (such as prior-season or split-half on/off or a rating model), starter share, opponent strength, score margin, pace and season fixed effects. The talent measure must not use the evaluated possessions or points-derived role labels. Fit random intercepts for team-season and cluster-robust standard errors.
design.falsification: (a) Permute role labels within team-season, preserving counts, to build a null for coverage variation and separability. (b) Swap the talent measure to a different team or season as a placebo, which should show a null coefficient. (c) Test role-label reliability by split-half agreement (target Cohen's kappa at or above 0.6 for assignments). (d) Re-run with outcome-free role definitions, and with thresholds shifted by plus or minus a pre-set margin.
design.multiplicity: Three primary diagnostics with fixed criteria, tested at alpha 0.05 with Holm correction. Role definitions, talent measure and possession minimum are pre-registered. All variants are reported as sensitivity analyses and given no confirmatory status.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if all of the following hold. (1) ICC for within-team variation: within-team-season share of coverage variance of at least 0.5 (threshold to be fixed before analysis), and coverage is neither near-constant nor near-universal (mean coverage between 0.15 and 0.85). (2) Separability: VIF below 5 and residual R-squared of coverage given counts and talent of at least 0.3. (3) The talent coefficient has the expected sign, its out-of-sample stability correlation is at least 0.6, and the placebo returns a null. If (1) fails, the answer is rejected or untestable. If (2) fails, the answer is that coverage is not separable. If role-label reliability fails, the answer is inconclusive. Report as untestable if too few lineups exceed the possession minimum.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons (playoffs separate), the derived graph-database play-type records, and 2025-26 as a frozen holdout once complete (regular season complete 2026-04-13, playoffs 2026-06-21). Freeze the data snapshot and record the extraction date and unit counts (420,993 possessions, 90 team-seasons) before analysis.
